subject: general
question: Which of the following cases CANNOT be taken up by a Lok Adalat?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Non-compoundable criminal offences**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lok Adalat** is a system of alternative dispute resolution in India where disputes are settled amicably through negotiation, mediation, and compromise.
 
• The cases that can be taken up by Lok Adalats include **civil cases, family disputes, labour disputes, motor accident claims, and other compoundable criminal offences.**
 
• **Non-compoundable criminal offences** are serious in nature and involve crimes that affect society at large, such as murder, rape, or dacoity. These cannot be compromised or settled outside court and hence, cannot be taken up by Lok Adalats.
 
• Such offences are dealt with under the purview of regular courts due to the severity of their consequences and the need for detailed legal proceedings.
 
• The **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**, under which Lok Adalats operate, specifies that only disputes that are not of a criminal nature or are compoundable can be resolved through Lok Adalats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Land acquisition cases**__

 __
 
• Land acquisition disputes often involve compensation-related grievances and other civil matters, which can be amicably settled in Lok Adalats.
 
• These cases are generally resolved quickly to ensure that the affected parties receive justice without prolonged litigation.
 
 
 
• **Motor accident claims**__
 __
 
• Motor accident claim cases, particularly those involving compensation for injuries or death, are often taken up by Lok Adalats for quick resolution.
 
• These cases typically involve insurance claims and require out-of-court settlements for the benefit of the victims and their families.
 
 
 
• **Divorce disputes under mutual consent**__
 
 
• Divorce cases under mutual consent are civil in nature and can be amicably resolved through Lok Adalats.
 
• Such cases involve agreement from both parties and do not require extensive legal proceedings, making them suitable for alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.
